slides.headline: India's first rocket parts arrived at the launch site by bicycle and bullock cart.
On November 21, 1963, India launched its first sounding rocket from Thumba, near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.
slides.body: The US-supplied Nike-Apache rocket carried a French payload, and a local church, St. Mary Magdalene, was converted into an early assembly facility and control room. Vikram Sarabhai and a young Abdul Kalam were both central to the launch.

slides.headline: That one rocket became the starting point for ISRO.
slides.body: The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station built around that first launch grew into the infrastructure base for India's entire space program, from early sounding rockets to Chandrayaan and Gaganyaan decades later.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat still runs on the same instinct that moved rocket parts by bullock cart - start with what you have.
slides.body: India's space program didn't begin with a launch pad. It began with a fishing village, a church, and two scientists willing to improvise their way to orbit.
